title: Phoenix chat template formatting can disclose server secrets
summary: Format string injection in applyChatTemplate can expose environment variables and PHOENIX_SECRET. That key enables session-token forgery and decryption of stored credentials.

severity.rationale: A reachable development and AI observability service can disclose administrator and model credentials. The documented impact warrants urgent credential protection.

exposure: The endpoint is unauthenticated in default no-auth deployments. With authentication enabled, any account is sufficient.

params.instructions: Check arize-phoenix version and whether the documented exposure conditions apply.

remediation.action: Update or contain the affected component
remediation.risk: Medium. Updates can interrupt workflows and require compatibility checks.

verification: Confirm the deployed component uses the patched release and test the affected workflow with harmless inputs.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record drafted from directly inspected primary sources for independent review.
